match.reason: The closest bank cards teach true bearings along with back bearings, navigation with the sine or cosine rule, or elevation, which is broader than this point's single idea of what a true bearing is, so a new point fits better.

draft.title: True bearings
card: A true bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north. It is written with three figures, so 45° is written 045°.
The four main directions are north 000°, east 090°, south 180° and west 270°.
A direction halfway between two of these is halfway between their bearings. North-west lies between west (270°) and north (360°), so it is 315°.
The bearing back is half a turn round. If the bearing from A to B is under 180°, add 180° to get the bearing from B to A. If it is 180° or more, subtract 180°.
draft.remember: Bearings start at north and turn clockwise. The way back is 180° different.

a.q: What is the true bearing of south-east?
a.why: South-east is halfway between east (090°) and south (180°), so it is 135°. 225° is tempting, but that is south-west, halfway between south and west.
a.clue: Find the angle halfway between east and south.

b.q: Lena walks from her camp to a lookout on a bearing of 305°. What is the bearing from the lookout back to the camp?
b.why: The bearing is over 180°, so subtract 180°: 305° − 180° = 125°. 055° is tempting, but it comes from 360° − 305°, which does not give the opposite direction.
b.clue: The way back is half a turn from the way out.

problems.detail: The card lists north as 000°, then uses north as 360° to find north-west without saying that 000° and 360° are the same direction. Students may be confused about why north changes value.

check.summary: Both questions and explanations are correct. One small wording issue: the card switches north from 000° to 360° without explaining that they are the same direction.
